rows.question: For Albany International, what was the year-end patent portfolio in aerospace technologies?
rows.answer: I could not find this in the reports. The reports I searched do not give a year-end patent count for aerospace technologies specifically. The only patent figure is company-wide: Albany's active portfolio "currently contains over 2,300 patents, and approximately 160 new patents are typically granted each year," and this is not broken out by aerospace [albany.pdf p.16]. The Albany Engineered Composites segment, which serves the commercial and defense aerospace industries, is described in [albany.pdf p.42], but no patent count is given for it.

rows.question: How many patents did Aurora Innovation hold at year end?
rows.answer:
Aurora Innovation did not report an issued-patent count. The report gives a combined figure: "As of December 31, 2022, we owned over 1,300 patents and pending applications, including U.S. and foreign." [aurora.pdf p.14]

So the 1,300+ figure includes pending applications and is not a count of granted patents alone. The report also says it has "6 registered U.S. trademarks, 32 registered foreign trademarks and 11 pending trademark applications." [aurora.pdf p.14]

rows.question: What was the non-performing loan ratio for FNCB Bancorp at year end?
rows.answer: FNCB Bancorp's ratio of non-performing loans to total gross loans was **0.25% at December 31, 2022**, down from 0.39% at December 31, 2021 [fncb.pdf p.52]. The shareholder letter gives the same figures: non-performing loans were $2.8 million, or 0.25% of total loans, at December 31, 2022 [fncb.pdf p.4].

rows.question: What was Albany International Corp.'s net cash provided by operating activities in 2022?
rows.answer: Albany International Corp.'s net cash provided by operating activities in 2022 was $128,214 thousand, or $128.2 million [albany.pdf p.61]. The MD&A states the same figure, $128.2 million in 2022, down from $217.5 million in 2021 [albany.pdf p.44].

rows.question: What was the amount paid in dividends by Albany International Corp. during 2022?
rows.answer: Albany International Corp. paid $26,465 thousand (about $26.5 million) in dividends in 2022. This is the "Dividends paid" line in the consolidated statements of cash flows [albany.pdf p.61]. The same report shows dividends declared of $0.88 per share for 2022 [albany.pdf p.58].

rows.question: What was Albany International Corp.'s effective tax rate for 2022?
rows.answer: Albany International Corp.'s effective tax rate for 2022 was 26.9%, down from 28.4% in 2021 [albany.pdf p.41]. The reconciliation to the U.S. federal statutory rate of 21.0% also shows 26.9% for 2022 [albany.pdf p.85]. Excluding discrete items, the rate was 30.7% [albany.pdf p.41].

rows.question: What was the amount of net cash used in investing activities for Armadale Capital Plc in 2022?
rows.answer:
For the year ended 31 December 2022, Armadale Capital Plc's consolidated net cash used in investing activities was **£(840) thousand** (2021: £(247) thousand) [armadale.pdf p.27].

This is the group figure. The parent company's own statement of cash flows shows a different number: net cash used in investing activities of **£(1,118) thousand** in 2022 (2021: £(673) thousand), driven by advances to subsidiaries [armadale.pdf p.28].

rows.question: What is the name of the self-driving platform developed by Aurora Innovation, Inc.?
rows.answer: Aurora Innovation, Inc. is developing the **Aurora Driver**, which the company describes as an advanced and scalable suite of self-driving hardware, software and data services designed as a platform to adapt and interoperate amongst vehicle types and applications [aurora.pdf p.67]. It is a common driver platform that has been integrated into numerous vehicle platforms, from passenger vehicles to light commercial vehicles to Class 8 trucks [aurora.pdf p.5].

rows.question: What was the amount of stock-based compensation recognized for related party RSUs by Aurora Innovation, Inc. for the year ended December 31, 2022?
rows.answer: Aurora Innovation, Inc. recognized $6 million in stock-based compensation for related party RSUs for the twelve months ended December 31, 2022 [aurora.pdf p.76]. No unrecognized stock-based compensation remained for these awards as of December 31, 2022 [aurora.pdf p.76].

rows.question: What was the valuation allowance at the end of the period for Aurora Innovation, Inc. as of December 31, 2022?
rows.answer: The valuation allowance at the end of the period for Aurora Innovation, Inc. as of December 31, 2022 was $542 million (in millions in the report). It rose from $331 million at the beginning of the period, driven by a change in deferred tax asset positions of $211 million [aurora.pdf p.81].

rows.question: What percentage of the ordinary share capital of Brave Bison Limited, Greenlight Digital Limited, and Greenlight Commerce Limited was transferred to Brave Bison 2021 Limited during the year?
rows.answer: The reports state that 100% of the ordinary share capital of Brave Bison Limited, Greenlight Digital Limited and Greenlight Commerce Limited was transferred to Brave Bison 2021 Limited during the year (year ended 31 December 2022) [brave-bison.pdf p.66]. The same statement appears in the consolidated undertakings note [brave-bison.pdf p.57].

rows.question: What was the revenue growth percentage for Brave Bison Group plc in 2022?
rows.answer: Brave Bison Group plc's revenue grew by 46% in 2022, to £31.7 million from £21.7 million in 2021 [brave-bison.pdf p.8]. The Results and Dividends section gives the same 46% increase, though it cites the 2021 base as £21.6 million [brave-bison.pdf p.26].

rows.question: What method does Brave Bison Group plc use to determine the fair value of equity instruments granted in share-based payment transactions?
rows.answer:
Brave Bison Group plc uses the Black-Scholes method to determine the fair value of equity instruments granted in share-based payment transactions. The cost of equity-settled transactions is measured by reference to fair value at the grant date, and the total value of the options is pro-rated and allocated on a weighted average basis [brave-bison.pdf p.45]. The company's parent-level share-based payment note says the same [brave-bison.pdf p.64].

For the 2022 grants, the Black-Scholes assumptions were an expected option life of 4 years, expected volatility of 50%, a risk-free interest rate of 0–1.25%, and an expected dividend yield of 0% [brave-bison.pdf p.56].

rows.question: What was the number of shares outstanding for FNCB Bancorp, Inc. as of March 11, 2023?
rows.answer: FNCB Bancorp, Inc. had 19,682,689 shares of common stock outstanding as of March 11, 2023 [fncb.pdf p.7]. This is the figure from the cover page of its annual report.

rows.question: What was FNCB Bancorp, Inc.'s tax-equivalent net interest margin in 2022?
rows.answer: FNCB Bancorp, Inc.'s tax-equivalent net interest margin was 3.38% in 2022. It declined seven basis points from 3.45% in 2021 [fncb.pdf p.40], [fncb.pdf p.3].

rows.question: What was the total number of shares bought back by Kelly Partners Group Holdings Limited from July 1, 2020, to April 7, 2021?
rows.answer:
Kelly Partners Group Holdings Limited bought back **400,000 shares** from July 1, 2020, to April 7, 2021.

The share movement note lists 16 buy-backs in that window, from 25 August 2020 to 7 April 2021. Summing them gives 400,000 [kelly-partners.pdf p.59]. The directors' report shows the same figure, "400k" shares repurchased in FY21 [kelly-partners.pdf p.5].

rows.question: What is the ownership percentage of Kelly Partners Wollongong Partnership for Kelly Partners Group Holdings Limited?
rows.answer: Kelly Partners Wollongong Partnership is 59.64% owned by Kelly Partners Group Holdings Limited at 30 June 2022 [kelly-partners.pdf p.80]. The same table shows 51.00% for 2021 [kelly-partners.pdf p.80].

rows.question: What was the revenue contribution of the acquired business by Kelly Partners Northern Beaches from 1 February 2022 to 30 June 2022?
rows.answer: The acquired accounting business of Kelly Partners Northern Beaches contributed revenues of $406,962 for the period from 1 February 2022 to 30 June 2022 [kelly-partners.pdf p.71]. The same report lists a separate acquisition, Kelly Partners Private Wealth (Northern Beaches), a wealth management business that contributed revenues of $196,910 over the same period [kelly-partners.pdf p.72]. Your question refers to Kelly Partners Northern Beaches, so the answer is $406,962.

rows.question: What is the total number of shares authorized for Common Stock by Wheeler Real Estate Investment Trust, Inc. as of December 31, 2022?
rows.answer: The total number of shares authorized for Common Stock by Wheeler Real Estate Investment Trust, Inc. as of December 31, 2022 was 200,000,000 shares, with $0.01 par value. The company's 215,000,000 total authorized stock includes that 200,000,000 common shares, along with preferred stock [wheeler.pdf p.78]. The balance sheet also states "200,000,000 shares authorized" for Common Stock [wheeler.pdf p.37].

rows.question: What is the trading symbol for the Notes issued by Wheeler Real Estate Investment Trust, Inc.?
rows.answer: The trading symbol for the Notes is **WHLRL**. The Notes are the 7.00% Subordinated Convertible Notes due 2031, listed on the Nasdaq Capital Market [wheeler.pdf p.1].

rows.question: What was the same store FFO increase for Wheeler Real Estate Investment Trust, Inc. during the year ended December 31, 2022?
rows.answer: Wheeler Real Estate Investment Trust, Inc.'s same store FFO increased by $2.80 million during the year ended December 31, 2022 [wheeler.pdf p.29]. The same store FFO table on that page shows $9,027 thousand in 2022 versus $6,225 thousand in 2021 [wheeler.pdf p.29].

rows.question: What was the principal amount of the Wilmington Financing Agreement entered into by Wheeler Real Estate Investment Trust, Inc. on March 12, 2021?
rows.answer: The Wilmington Financing Agreement, which Wheeler Real Estate Investment Trust, Inc. entered into on March 12, 2021, provided for a term loan in the aggregate principal amount of $35.00 million [wheeler.pdf p.54]. It carried an 8.00% rate and matured in March 2026 [wheeler.pdf p.54].

rows.question: What was the aggregate cost of the Series D Preferred shares purchased by Wheeler Real Estate Investment Trust, Inc. on March 12, 2021?
rows.answer: Wheeler Real Estate Investment Trust, Inc. bought 387,097 shares of Series D Preferred on March 12, 2021, at $15.50 per share, for an aggregate cost of $6.00 million, excluding fees and expenses [wheeler.pdf p.61]. That purchase came from the modified Dutch auction tender offer, which the company also describes as having an aggregate cost of $6.00 million [wheeler.pdf p.23].

rows.question: How much did Albany International Corp. spend on research and development for advanced programs?
rows.answer:
The reports don't use the term "advanced programs." The closest figures are the research and development spending for the Albany Engineered Composites (AEC) segment, which is the advanced-materials business:

- **AEC segment internally funded R&D: $15,353 thousand in 2022** ($12,891 thousand in 2021; $9,828 thousand in 2020) [albany.pdf p.39]
- The AEC figure of $15.4 million in 2022 was 3.6 percent of AEC Net sales [albany.pdf p.16]

If you meant total company spending, it was $31.4 million in 2022 (3.0 percent of Net sales), of which $16,060 thousand was Machine Clothing [albany.pdf p.16, p.39].

rows.question: Did Brave Bison Group plc report any mergers or acquisitions during the year?
rows.answer:
Yes. Brave Bison Group plc acquired Best Response Media Limited during 2022:

- **Date and business:** The Group acquired the entire issued share capital of Best Response Media Limited on 28 April 2022. It is a specialist ecommerce and mobile development company focused on the Adobe Commerce Platform. [brave-bison.pdf p.61]
- **Consideration:** £1,174k in total, made up of £962k initial cash paid, a £37k completion accounts adjustment paid, and £175k deferred cash paid. The consideration was financed from existing cash balances. [brave-bison.pdf p.61]
- **Strategic rationale:** The acquisition let the Group offer services on Adobe Commerce Cloud and brought in a resource base in Mansoura, Egypt, and Tier 1 customers including NatWest. [brave-bison.pdf p.6]
- **Contribution:** Best Response Media contributed £0.5 million of revenue and a £0.2 million loss to the Group for the period from acquisition to the year end. [brave-bison.pdf p.61]
- **Costs:** Acquisition costs were £0.1 million in 2022, compared with £0.7 million in 2021. [brave-bison.pdf p.8]

The annual report describes this as the Group's third acquisition since mid-2020. [brave-bison.pdf p.6] The report also says the purchase price allocation for Best Response Media was provisional, with the full valuation to be completed within one year of the acquisition date. [brave-bison.pdf p.46]

rows.question: Which leadership position changed at Kelly Partners Group Holdings Limited in the reporting period?
rows.answer:
I could not find a leadership position that changed during the reporting period (the year ended 30 June 2022). The only board change in the report is a post-period appointment.

- **Lawrence Cunningham** was appointed Non-Executive Independent Director on 1 July 2022 [kelly-partners.pdf p.14], which is after the 30 June 2022 year end. The report lists it as a matter subsequent to the end of the financial year [kelly-partners.pdf p.14], and his biography appears in the directors' report [kelly-partners.pdf p.17].

The report also lists Brett Kelly as Executive Chairman and Chief Executive Officer [kelly-partners.pdf p.15], Stephen Rouvray as Deputy Chairman [kelly-partners.pdf p.16], and Joyce Au as company secretary [kelly-partners.pdf p.3]. I found nothing showing these roles changed in the period.

rows.question: What was Wheeler Real Estate Investment Trust's cash flow from operations for the year?
rows.answer: Wheeler Real Estate Investment Trust's cash flow from operating activities was $30,758 thousand (about $30.8 million) for the year ended December 31, 2022, up from $17,041 thousand in 2021 [wheeler.pdf p.21].

rows.question: What was Albany International's total revenue in fiscal year 2027?
rows.answer:
I could not find fiscal year 2027 revenue in the reports. The Albany International report provided covers fiscal years 2018 to 2022, so it contains no 2027 figures.

The most recent total revenue in the report is for fiscal 2022: consolidated net sales of $1,034,887 thousand (about $1.03 billion) [albany.pdf p.38]. The report labels this line "Net sales," and its financial highlights call it "Total Revenue" [albany.pdf p.3].

rows.question: What did FNCB Bancorp pay in cyber insurance premiums last year?
rows.answer:
I could not find this in the reports.

I searched the FNCB Bancorp 2022 annual report for cyber insurance premium payments using several phrasings, and I did not find any figure for them. The closest material was:

- The cyber-attack risk factor says FNCB "has not incurred a material cyber-attack or security breach to date," but it gives no insurance cost [fncb.pdf p.26].
- The related party note mentions "fidelity bond and errors and omissions insurance" bought from related parties, with total related-party payments of $0.5 million in 2022 and $2.0 million in 2021. It does not break out cyber insurance [fncb.pdf p.104].
- The income statement's "Other operating expenses" line was $4,976 thousand in 2022, but the report does not itemize it, so it cannot be used to isolate cyber premiums [fncb.pdf p.68].

The report is the 2022 10-K, which matches "last year" as far as I can tell. I did not check the full notes for a more specific insurance breakdown, so a cyber premium figure may exist elsewhere in the filing that my searches did not surface.

rows.question: What is Wheeler Real Estate Investment Trust's average tenant satisfaction score?
rows.answer: I could not find this in the reports. I searched the Wheeler Real Estate Investment Trust report (wheeler.pdf) for "average tenant satisfaction score" and related terms such as "tenant satisfaction survey," "customer satisfaction rating," and "net promoter," and none of the results mention a tenant satisfaction score. rows.question: Which law firm advised Kelly Partners on its most recent acquisition?
rows.answer:

The Kelly Partners annual report (30 June 2022) describes its acquisitions and the costs of implementing them, including "legal costs," but it does not name the law firm that advised on any acquisition [kelly-partners.pdf p.12]. The most recent acquisitions it covers are the Dungog accounting firm completed 1 July 2022 and the Leeton accounting firm agreements signed 21 July 2022 [kelly-partners.pdf p.15; kelly-partners.pdf p.84]. Neither passage names an adviser.

rows.question: What are Armadale Capital's proven gold reserves in Tanzania?
rows.answer: I could not find this in the reports. The Armadale Capital annual report for the year ended 31 December 2022 (armadale.pdf) describes its key Tanzanian asset as the Mahenge Liandu Graphite Project, a graphite project, not a gold project [armadale.pdf p.4][armadale.pdf p.5]. I found no proven gold reserve figures for Tanzania. The only gold reference is a royalty on gold production from a previously held gold project, with no reserve figures given [armadale.pdf p.7].

rows.question: How many hours of safety training did FNCB Bancorp deliver per employee?
rows.answer: I could not find this in the reports. I searched the FNCB Bancorp annual report (fncb.pdf) for safety training hours per employee using several queries, and nothing relevant came up. The closest material is the "Human Capital Resources" section, which describes employee count (230 persons as of December 31, 2022) and a statement that FNCB is "investing in employee training and leadership programs," but it gives no safety training hours figure [fncb.pdf p.19; fncb.pdf p.6].

rows.question: What is the average age of Wheeler Real Estate Investment Trust's shopping centres?
rows.answer: I could not find this in the reports. The searches returned property lists, Schedule III depreciation tables, lease statistics, and the portfolio overview, but none states an average age for the shopping centres. The Item 2 property table I opened is cut off after the first two properties, so it may contain build or acquisition years, but I did not see them. The Schedule III table gives acquisition dates for each centre (for example, Tuckernuck 11/16/2012 and JANAF Shopping Center 1/18/2018 [wheeler.pdf p.70, p.71]), but computing an average from those would be my own calculation, not a figure the company reports.

rows.question: What did Kelly Partners Group pay its auditor for tax advice in 2019?
rows.answer:
I could not find this in the reports. The only Kelly Partners Group report available is the FY2022 annual report (year ended 30 June 2022), which covers 2022 and 2021 only, not 2019.

Its auditor-fees note (Note 32) lists only two categories for William Buck Accountants & Advisors: audit or review of the financial statements ($86,600 in 2022; $71,150 in 2021), and audit of operating business trust accounts ($5,465 in 2022; $6,020 in 2021) [kelly-partners.pdf p.65]. No tax advice or other tax-service fees appear in either year.

rows.question: How many charging stations does Aurora Innovation operate?
rows.answer: I could not find this in the reports. I searched the Aurora Innovation annual report (aurora.pdf) for charging stations, EV charging, depots and facilities, and found no mention of a count of charging stations. The report describes Aurora as a self-driving technology company developing the Aurora Driver [aurora.pdf p.67], so it does not appear to disclose this figure.

rows.question: What was Armadale Capital Plc's gross margin for the year?
rows.answer: I could not find a gross margin for Armadale Capital Plc in the reports. The consolidated statement of comprehensive income for the year ended 31 December 2022 has no revenue or cost of sales lines, so no gross profit can be calculated. It shows administrative expenses of £(309)_000 and a change in fair value of investments of £103_000, giving an operating loss of £(206)_000 [armadale.pdf p.22]. The company is an exploration company: its Tanzania project has not commenced production, and its exploration costs are capitalised [armadale.pdf p.40, p.42].

rows.answer: I could not find this in the reports. The Albany International annual report describes the company's ongoing commitment to new product development. For example, it says the Machine Clothing research team "develops new products to meet changes in customer needs" [albany.pdf p.17], and that "This innovation has resulted in new MC products and/or enhancements across all of our product lines" [albany.pdf p.16]. It also says Albany Engineered Composites is "continu[ing] to invest in the next generation of composite materials and their industrialization" [albany.pdf p.5]. However, none of the passages I retrieved name a specific product that was launched during the year, so I cannot list the new products.

Its Item 2 Properties section describes "principal manufacturing facilities" in Brazil, Canada, China, France, Germany, Italy, Mexico, South Korea, Sweden, the United Kingdom, and the United States, but gives no count of facilities [albany.pdf p.32]. Searches for fulfillment centres or fulfillment centers returned no relevant passages.

rows.question: How many hotels did Wheeler Real Estate Investment Trust own at year end?

It describes the company as owning and operating retail properties, with "seventy-five centers and four undeveloped properties" at December 31, 2022 [wheeler.pdf p.41]. Searches for "hotel" and "hospitality" in the Wheeler report returned no matching passages.
